title: Q-Learning With World Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.17163v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Off-policy reinforcement learning (RL) has become increasingly sample-efficient, enabling applications such as RL fine-tuning of Vision-Language-Action models into reliable, high-performing policies. World models offer a further lever for sample efficiency, as they predict state changes rather than actions alone, but their success has largely been confined to supervised policy learning. Prior model-based RL methods often optimize the policy or value function directly on imagined rollouts, which is prone to compounding bias and struggles to scale to large, high-dimensional problems such as real-world robotics, a problem that worsens with task horizon and visual complexity. In this work, we instead ask whether we can leverage world models directly on top of standard Q-learning to improve performance, while remaining trained and grounded in the real, online setting. translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.17163v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：离策略强化学习（RL）已成为越来越样本高效的方法，使得诸如将视觉-语言-动作模型微调为可靠、高性能策略的应用成为可能。世界模型提供了进一步提升样本效率的杠杆，因为它们预测状态变化而非仅预测动作，但其成功在很大程度上局限于监督策略学习。先前的基于模型的强化学习方法通常直接在想象的轨迹上优化策略或价值函数，这容易导致复合偏差，并难以扩展到大规模、高维问题（如真实世界机器人），且随着任务时长和视觉复杂性的增加，该问题会加剧。在本工作中，我们转而探讨是否可以在标准Q学习之上直接利用世界模型来提升性能，同时保持在真实在线环境中训练和基于真实数据。我们提出了QWM框架，该框架利用世界模型进行测试时...
tldr: 本文提出QWM框架，通过将世界模型直接集成到标准Q学习中，在真实在线环境中提升强化学习性能，避免基于想象轨迹的复合偏差问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the QWM framework, which integrates world models directly into standard Q-learning to improve RL performance in the real online setting, avoiding the compounding bias issue from imagined rollouts.
